title: Minimum Number of Operations to Move All Balls to Each Box
statement:
The string `boxes` describes a row of `n` boxes: character `i` is `'1'` when box `i` holds a single ball and `'0'` when it is empty. A single operation takes one ball and shifts it into a neighbouring box (index differing by exactly 1); a box may end up holding several balls.

Return an array `answer` of length `n` in which `answer[i]` is the fewest operations that gather every ball into box `i`. Each entry is computed independently, always starting from the original arrangement in `boxes`.
notes:
## Intuition

The direct way sums `|i - j|` over every ball `j` for each target `i`, which is O(n²). Split the cost for box `i` into the balls on its left and the balls on its right. When the target moves one box to the right, every ball already on its left must travel one more step, so the left cost grows by exactly the number of balls seen so far. The same holds from the right, so two sweeps give every answer.

## Approach

1. Make `answer` full of zeros and set `balls = 0`, `cost = 0`.
2. Sweep left to right. Store `cost` (moving every ball strictly left of `i` into box `i`) in `answer[i]`.
3. If box `i` has a ball, increase `balls`. Then add `balls` to `cost`: stepping to `i + 1` moves each of them one more box.
4. Reset `balls` and `cost`, sweep right to left the same way, and add `cost` to `answer[i]`.
5. Return `answer`.

## Example 1, step by step

`boxes = "110"`. Left sweep: `i = 0` stores 0, then `balls = 1`, `cost = 1`; `i = 1` stores 1, then `balls = 2`, `cost = 3`; `i = 2` stores 3. So `answer = [0, 1, 3]`. Right sweep: `i = 2` adds 0 (box 2 is empty, `cost` stays 0); `i = 1` adds 0, then `balls = 1`, `cost = 1`; `i = 0` adds 1. Result `[1, 1, 3]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): two passes over the string, constant work per box.
- Space: O(1) besides the returned array.

## Pitfalls

- Store `cost` into `answer[i]` before counting box `i`'s own ball; that ball needs no moves to reach box `i`.
- Reset both `balls` and `cost` before the second sweep.
- The second sweep must add to `answer[i]`, not overwrite it.
- Characters are `'0'` and `'1'` strings, so compare with `'1'`, not the number 1.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | number of boxes |
| `answer` | operations needed for each target box |
| `balls` | balls seen so far in the current sweep |
| `cost` | moves to bring all those balls to the current box |
| `i` | the current target box |

narration.3: One answer per box, starting at zero.
narration.4: Count of balls seen so far in the current sweep.
narration.5: Moves needed to bring those balls to the current box.
narration.7: First sweep: from left to right.
narration.8: Record what it costs to bring every ball on the left into box i.
narration.9: Does box i hold a ball?
narration.10: Yes: from now on it also has to travel.
narration.12: Stepping one box to the right moves every counted ball one more step.
narration.15: Start the second sweep with no balls counted.
narration.17: Second sweep: from right to left.
narration.18: Add the cost of bringing every ball on the right into box i.
narration.22: Stepping one box to the left moves every counted ball one more step.
narration.24: Each entry now holds the left cost plus the right cost.
